Table of Contents
1 Introduction
1.1 Purpose

Enterprise RAG Assistant answers employee questions from approved company documents. This SRS defines its required behaviour, permissions, interfaces, data rules, and quality targets. It gives the owner, developer, tester, and course reviewer a common basis for implementation and acceptance.
The owner uses the SRS to control scope. Developers use Section 3 to implement the system; testers and reviewers use Section 6 to check coverage and record results.
1.2 Scope

The assistant accepts questions in English and returns answers supported by documents the employee may access. A substantive answer includes a source citation. If the available evidence is insufficient, the system returns a generic not-found result.

Version 1 covers offline Markdown and text-based PDF ingestion, department tagging, signed-token login, restricted question answering, a REST API, browser chat, query metrics, evaluation, and a deployed demo. Acme Corp is a fictional company represented by selected public GitLab Handbook pages.

Voice, multilingual support, native mobile apps, model training, document editing through chat, live company-system synchronisation, SSO, and multi-tenant hosting are excluded. OCR for scanned PDFs is a possible later extension.

1.5 Overview

Section 2 sets the product context and release boundary. Section 3 specifies behaviour and quality. Sections 4 and 5 govern changes and approval. Section 6 holds verification, traceability, provenance, and unresolved decisions.
2 The Overall Description
2.1 Product Perspective

The assistant serves one organisation and supplements its document collection. It does not edit policies or perform the payroll, leave, purchasing, or other transactions described in them. Employees follow the cited policy and its existing approval process.

The system includes ingestion, authentication, access filtering, retrieval, generation, citation checking, the API, chat, logging, and evaluation. It reads approved files offline. At query time, the external model service receives the question and authorised evidence; the assistant does not browse the live handbook.

2.1.1 System Interfaces

The employee interface uses the API for login and questions. Ingestion reads local files; evaluation exercises the system under recorded roles. Version 1 has no payroll, HR-system, SSO-provider, or live document-management integration.
2.1.2 User Interfaces

Employees use login and chat screens showing questions, answers, citations, and request outcomes. They cannot assign themselves another role or add files to the approved collection. Operators use command-line ingestion and evaluation tools.
2.1.3 Hardware Interfaces
No specialised hardware interfaces are required. The application uses ordinary storage, networking, and a browser; it does not control external devices.
2.1.4 Software Interfaces

The backend exchanges requests with a hosted model service. R4 selects Groq behind a replaceable client interface. Storage engines, retrieval libraries, and the UI framework are internal design choices. Provider versions and limits are deployment settings subject to OD-03 and OD-04.
2.1.5 Communications Interfaces

The deployed client and API communicate over HTTPS; authenticated requests carry a bearer token. The backend needs outbound access to the model provider. No custom device or messaging protocol is used.
2.1.6 Memory Constraints
RAM, storage, throughput, and concurrent-user limits are not yet baselined. They will be measured against the selected models, document collection, and host under OD-01.
2.1.7 Operations

The operator prepares documents offline while serving is stopped. After ingestion, the service restarts and checks consistency between the chunk collection and retrieval indexes. Employees then log in and ask questions. Evaluation is a separate operator-run activity.
Retention, backup, and recovery arrangements remain open under OD-02. Continuous service during document updates is outside the first-release commitment.
2.1.8 Site Adaptation Requirements

The operator configures source paths, department mapping, accounts, provider credentials, storage, retrieval settings, and content logging. Private company deployment also requires an agreed access map and approval of the provider data flow. No physical site changes are required.
2.2 Product Functions
Prepare an approved document collection and preserve its department and source metadata.
Authenticate employees and determine their permissions from a backend-verified token.
Find relevant passages within the departments permitted for the employee.
Produce an evidence-based answer with validated citations, or return a generic not-found outcome.
Expose the behaviour through an API and chat interface.
Record operational metrics and compare answer quality across retrieval configurations.
2.3 User Characteristics

Employees need English reading skills and ordinary browser experience, not knowledge of retrieval or language models. The roles below determine permissions, not technical skill. The operator must be able to configure the deployment and run its command-line tools.
Operator is a maintenance responsibility, not a fifth employee role. The handbook is public; its access restrictions are simulated for this project.
2.4 Constraints
The first release serves one organisation with four employee roles and department-level permissions.
Permission checks occur in the backend before evidence reaches answer generation. Client controls and prompts cannot grant access.
The serving process uses one API worker. Document ingestion is performed offline.
The demo collection is pinned to a recorded handbook commit. Dataset provenance and attribution are retained.
External service availability and account limits affect generation and evaluation.
Secrets, logs, local datasets, virtual environments, and generated databases are excluded from the public source repository.
2.5 Assumptions and Dependencies

The baseline comes from the owner’s goals and project specification; no enterprise stakeholder interview has been completed. The operator is responsible for source accuracy, approval, and classification.

Employees need a browser and network access; generation depends on the model provider. Roles are trusted only after backend verification. A revoked account may retain access until its token expires; immediate revocation is deferred.
Quality targets remain provisional until the environment and scoring protocol are recorded. Changes to these assumptions follow Section 4.

3.2 System Features and Functional Requirements
Each feature states its purpose and operating context, followed by requirements and acceptance criteria. Original IDs are retained for traceability to R3.
3.2.1 Document Ingestion and Classification
Purpose. Prepare approved documents while retaining source identity and department classification.

Operating context. The operator runs ingestion while serving is stopped. The folder must be readable and source paths mapped. Ingestion extracts text, prepares labelled chunks, updates changed documents, and removes deleted sources.
FR-01 Supported document ingestion
The system shall ingest Markdown documents and text-based PDF documents from a configured local data folder.

Acceptance. AT-01: ingest one readable Markdown fixture and one text-based PDF fixture; confirm that their body text is available in the prepared collection and remains associated with the source file. Scanned PDFs are outside the required set.
FR-02 Department and source metadata
The system shall associate each ingested document and its derived chunks with a department and source metadata that supports access enforcement and source citation.

Acceptance. AT-02: verify department, document identity, source path, checksum, title, and section or page metadata for prepared fixtures; reject a source that cannot be assigned an approved department.

Exception handling. Malformed, excluded, or unmapped paths receive no default department. Ingestion errors must not expose unclassified content. Corrupt-file handling and partial-run reporting remain OD-04.
3.2.2 Authentication and Role Enforcement
Purpose. Authenticate employees and enforce their permissions before evidence reaches generation.

Operating context. A valid demo account has an assigned role. Login issues a signed token; the backend verifies it on each question and selects permitted departments. Unknown roles receive no fallback access. The design sets a 30-minute expiry.
FR-11 Signed-token authentication
The system shall authenticate an employee and determine the employee’s role from a signed token verified by the backend.

Acceptance. AT-11: valid credentials produce a usable signed token; altered, invalid, and expired tokens cannot authorise a question. A role supplied in the question body cannot change the role determined by the token.
FR-05 Retrieval within permitted departments
The system shall supply retrieval evidence only from documents within the authenticated employee’s permitted departments.

Acceptance. AT-05: for each role, inspect retrieved chunks and the complete model request; every passage must belong to an allowed department. A search dominated by disallowed documents must still consider permitted candidates before selecting the final results.
FR-12 Indistinguishable restricted and missing outcomes
The system shall return the same generic not-found reply when requested evidence is restricted and when it does not exist in the approved collection.

Acceptance. AT-12: ask equivalent questions about a known restricted source and a non-existent source as the same role; compare the public found flag, answer message, and citations. The not-found result must not disclose the restricted title or its existence.
3.2.3 Question Answering and Evidence Sufficiency
Purpose. Answer from permitted evidence and refuse unsupported conclusions.

Operating context. An authenticated employee submits a question to a ready service. Relevant permitted passages are assessed for sufficiency. Insufficient evidence produces not found; supported generation proceeds to citation checking.
FR-03 Answers grounded in retrieved documents
The system shall answer a natural-language question using the retrieved document content as its source of factual evidence.

Acceptance. AT-03: submit factual and multi-section questions with expected answers derived from approved sources; assess answer correctness and source support using the evaluation method defined for NFR-02.
FR-06 Refusal when evidence is insufficient
The system shall return a not-found outcome when the permitted retrieved evidence does not support an answer.

Acceptance. AT-06: below-threshold evidence stops generation; an insufficient-context result from generation also becomes not found. Questions outside the collection must not produce a factual answer based solely on model knowledge.
FR-10 Resistance to instruction overrides
The system shall preserve its access rules and evidence-based answering behaviour when a question or retrieved document contains instructions that attempt to override them.

Acceptance. AT-10: test instructions embedded in questions and document passages that request another role, restricted sources, unsupported answers, or invented citations. Inspect both the public result and the model input; no restricted passage may be supplied.
3.2.4 Citation Validation and Answer Delivery
Purpose. Trace each substantive answer to evidence actually supplied for generation.

Operating context. The generator returns an answer and citation IDs. The system retains only IDs from the supplied chunks. If none remain, it suppresses the answer and returns not found without another model call to repair citations.
FR-04 Readable source citations
The system shall include at least one citation identifying the document title and section or PDF page in every substantive answer returned to an employee.

Acceptance. AT-04: each successful found=true response includes a citation with a document title and section or page that resolves to supplied evidence. A not-found response is not a substantive answer and requires no invented citation.
FR-13 Citation identifier validation
The system shall validate every proposed citation against the chunks supplied to the model, discard invalid identifiers, and return not found when no valid citation remains.

Acceptance. AT-13: all-valid identifiers are retained; mixed valid and invalid identifiers retain only valid entries; all-invalid or empty identifiers produce not found. Confirm that citation repair does not trigger another model call.
FR-07 API and chat access
The system shall make question answering available through a REST API and a browser-based chat interface.

Acceptance. AT-07: authenticate and ask the same supported question through each interface; confirm equivalent access restrictions, answer outcome, and citation requirements. Confirm that ingestion and evaluation remain operator tools rather than employee API functions.
3.2.5 Query Logging and Evaluation
Purpose. Record query metrics and measure the quality and safety of answering.

Operating context. Query completion writes metrics under the configured privacy setting. An operator runs evaluation under recorded roles and reports outcomes against the pinned dataset and configuration.
FR-08 Query metrics with controlled content logging
The system shall record query role, retrieved chunk identifiers, relevance scores, latency, and token count; it shall store question and answer text only when content logging is enabled.

Acceptance. AT-08: with content logging disabled, required metric fields are present and question/answer text is absent. With it enabled, text may be recorded. Logged role values are bounded and sanitised. The client-deployment default is content logging off.
FR-09 Repeatable evaluation report
The system shall provide an evaluation script that runs the defined test-question set and reports the resulting scores.

Acceptance. AT-09: provide a valid evaluation file, run it as each recorded role, and obtain traceable per-question and aggregate results. Record the dataset revision, configuration, scoring method, and unresolved or failed questions.

Evaluation uses bounded concurrency, backoff for provider rate limits, and resumable cached results as specified in R4. Cache reuse must preserve role, source-revision, and configuration boundaries. Numeric settings remain open.
3.2.6 Business Rules

rows: The only employee roles are new_hire, hr, finance, and engineer. Allowed departments are exactly those in Section 2.3. Unknown roles fail closed.
Department assignment follows the longest matching source-path prefix. An explicit file mapping overrides its parent folder. An unmapped source is refused.

Paths are relative and use forward slashes. Segments allow ASCII letters, digits, period, underscore, and hyphen. Traversal, empty segments, trailing dots or spaces, and excluded prefixes are refused.
Access restriction applies to vector and keyword results before final candidate selection and before any passage reaches the model.
The not-found threshold uses reranker relevance when enabled, otherwise best vector similarity. A fused RRF score is not the sufficiency measure. Each configuration has a calibrated threshold.
Citations identify only chunks supplied for the current generation. Invalid identifiers are removed; no valid citation means not found.
A changed or deleted document loses its obsolete chunks during offline ingestion. Unchanged documents need not be embedded again.
The demo selection contains 190 pages: engineering 60, finance 35, people 50, onboarding 5, and general 40. Each selected page has at least 150 real words by the documented selection method.

text: finance/readmes and finance/jihu-support are excluded case-insensitively. Approved mapping matches are case-sensitive; the complete path map remains in R5.
3.3 Performance Requirements
The following targets are provisional. The measured environment, workload, scoring method, and cost basis must be recorded before a pass is declared.

The evaluated system shall achieve faithfulness of at least 0.85 and answer correctness of at least 75% on the agreed test questions.

QT-01: retain per-question scores and aggregate results. The scoring rubric, scoring model if used, treatment of refusals, and denominator must be approved under OD-05 before a pass can be declared. Source: R3 NFR-02.
The average language-model charge shall not exceed USD 0.02 per evaluated question.

CT-01: divide total billed generation cost by the evaluated question count and retain token usage and the price basis used for that run. State whether evaluation-judge calls are excluded. The accounting boundary remains OD-05. Source: R3 NFR-04.

3.6 Software System Attributes
3.6.1 Reliability

FR-06 refuses unsupported questions, FR-13 suppresses answers without valid citations, and DR-05 blocks inconsistent serving data. QT-01 evaluates the support for generated claims. No MTBF target has been agreed.
Provider and infrastructure failures are service errors, not evidence that an answer is absent. Recovery and timeout behaviour remain OD-04.
3.6.2 Availability

The demo depends on its host and model provider. Updates stop and restart the service. No uptime percentage, recovery-time objective, or recovery-point objective is approved; OD-02 and OD-06 cover these decisions.
3.6.3 Security and Privacy

rows: The system shall disclose no restricted document content across the defined access-control acceptance questions. [R3 NFR-03]
ST-01: inspect answers, citations, retrieved evidence, and model payloads for all role-denial cases. Any leak fails acceptance for the test set.
No API key, signing secret, password, or other deployment secret shall be committed to the project repository. [R3 NFR-07]
ST-02: inspect tracked files and configuration examples for secrets; confirm sensitive local artifacts are excluded. Record the inspection scope.

text: Access security is specified by FR-05 and FR-10 to FR-13. A public not-found result must not expose a restricted source. Client deployments disable content logging by default; automatic personal-data masking is deferred.

The design expires tokens after 30 minutes; immediate revocation is not guaranteed. Credential protection, provisioning, signing, browser token handling, and provider data handling remain OD-03 and OD-04.
3.6.4 Maintainability

The design uses replaceable model and vector-store interfaces and one role-policy table. A component change must preserve access, refusal, and citation behaviour and pass the affected acceptance checks.
No numerical complexity, coverage, or repair-time target is agreed. Maintainability review checks interface separation and continued use of the acceptance procedures.

The system shall support Markdown and text-based PDF source documents. Scanned PDFs are not required. [R3 NFR-05]

IR-01 defines the basic employee interactions. A measured usability target and accessibility conformance level are not approved; OD-07 records the required decisions.

3.7 Organisation of Specific Requirements

Section 3.2 follows the template’s feature organisation. Its alternative outlines by mode, user class, object, stimulus, response, functional hierarchy, and use case are not additional required functions and are not duplicated.
3.8 Additional Comments

Not found is distinct from invalid authentication, invalid input, and service failure. Citation membership confirms which evidence was supplied; faithfulness evaluation checks whether that evidence supports the answer.
4 Change Management Process
4.1 Submitting a Change

A change request is recorded in a repository issue or equivalent written record. It identifies affected IDs, revised wording, the reason, and expected scope impact. Informal discussion alone does not alter the baseline.
4.2 Impact Assessment

The owner reviews the effect on permissions, data, interfaces, implementation, verification, cost, and schedule. Access changes require revised denial tests. Performance changes need an agreed protocol or measurements.
4.3 Decision and Approval

Abdul Samad records acceptance, rejection, or deferral of each request. Changes to an academically approved baseline are submitted to the course reviewer when review is required. This procedure takes effect on document approval.
4.4 Updating the Baseline

An accepted change updates the requirement, verification, traceability, relevant design, and revision history. Unchanged obligations retain their IDs; withdrawn IDs are not reused. Approved document versions are retained with their implementation and test references.

5 Document Approvals
Approval records agreement on the identified document version. Signatures and dates remain blank until review. Academic approval does not represent enterprise-customer approval.
5.1 Approval Conditions
Review covers scope, clarity, permissions, sources, and verification. A draft may retain open decisions, but operational acceptance must identify their resolution or explicit deferral.
5.2 Release Acceptance Record
Product acceptance is recorded separately after testing. The record identifies the product revision, dataset, configuration, environment, procedures, results, unresolved defects, and final decision.

6.4 Data Provenance and Attribution

The dataset uses GitLab Handbook commit 2c77a1f5b8c8a80cb7b5151ff11cfad84f98bfbb, downloaded on 11 October 2026 according to R5. Selected files are copied unchanged to the local department folders and excluded from Git.

Each selected page has at least 150 real words after the documented exclusions. Deterministic round-robin selection spreads topics; the manifest is sorted by source path. SHA-256 checksums normalise CRLF to LF.

Dataset attribution: GitLab Handbook, GitLab, https://handbook.gitlab.com, source repository https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/content-sites/handbook, licensed as recorded by the project under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/. The SRS describes the application and does not reproduce handbook policy text.
6.5 Implementation Context

The reviewed source implements role permissions, department-path mapping, deterministic page selection, checksums, and Markdown chunking with front-matter removal. Title extraction and the complete citation metadata are still in progress.
The API, chat, storage, retrieval, generation, logging, evaluation, Docker setup, and live demo remain planned work. Their inclusion in the SRS states the intended release, not completed delivery.
